text:
maria: FYI customer (tenant: pico-retail) on Dedicated hit sustained 429s and timeouts during a traffic spike, says scale didn't keep up. raising for triage :eyes:

jake: can you paste the customer-request-id and a short timeline? 429s could be probe throttles or attach backlog.

maria: asked them for the x-request-id, got `req-9c3f2a`. timeline: 13:02 -> sudden 3x QPS, 13:03 errors spike, 13:07 still elevated. They said min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20, target_rps per pod ~100.

olivia: customer says they saw an auth failure earlier at 12:59 (billing rotation) but it recovered. not sure if related. I can share chat logs privately.

sam: quick checks — can someone grep attach/queue metrics for that tenant around 13:00? also need autoscaler logs for hysteresis events.

maria: pasted minimal repro: curl to their endpoint with ramp script. sample log from edge (13:03):
```
2026-01-22T13:03:12Z ERROR http: 429 Too Many Requests tenant=pico-retail route=/v1/generate attempt=1 pool=dedicated-us-east-3
2026-01-22T13:03:13Z WARN autoscaler: scale_request suppressed due_to=hysteresis last_scale=70s recommended=6
```

jake: that `suppressed` line is interesting — looks like the autoscaler saw a previous scale event and backed off. need `autoscaler-controller` logs and the probe heartbeat timings. also check warm-pool occupancy.

autoscaler-bot: pulled logs for tenant pico-retail between 2026-01-22T12:56:00Z and 2026-01-22T13:10:00Z — uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-logs/pico-retail/1768003333-autoscaler.tgz :link:

sam: grabbing those now. initial glance: warm-pool nodes for this tenant were at 0 at 12:58, then 1 at 13:05. so warm-pool cold. image pulls show a few backoffs around 13:01 — possibly registry pull congestion causing delayed attach.

olivia: customer mentioned noisy neighbors on the same Dedicated cluster earlier this week, could be resource contention during image pull. they also saw transient 401 around 12:59 (auth rotation) — maybe aborting some attach flows.

jake: two-pronged hypothesis: 1) attach queue growth due to auth rotation causing attach failures; 2) autoscaler hysteresis/holdoff prevented rapid scaleup while queue grew. both together caused sustained 429s.

maria: repro steps I'm putting in the ticket so support can run:
1) set min_replicas=2 max_replicas=20, target_rps=100
2) start ramp script: `for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "x-customer-id: pico-retail" http://dedicated-us-east:8080/v1/generate & done`
3) simulate auth rotation by toggling service-account secret for tenant for 30s before ramp
4) monitor `/metrics` for `attach_queue_length`, `warm_pool_size`, and autoscaler `last_scale_time`

sam: to triage right now I recommend:
- check registry pull rates and image cache hits for that node pool (kubelet logs)
- confirm KMS/key rotation timestamps for that tenant (auth failures)
- bump warm_pool_target to 2 temporarily for this tenant and re-run ramp (will cost them but lets us repro)
- collect `kubectl describe pod` for any pods that failed to attach around 13:00

maria: doing the warm_pool bump with customer approval. pinging infra to check registry throttling.

jake: also check autoscaler params: `scale_down_delay`, `scale_up_cooldown`, `stabilization_window`. if scale_up_cooldown is high we can get this hysteresis. wonder if their custom policy has `stabilization_window=120s`.

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler config for tenant pico-retail: `min=2 max=20 target_rps=100 stabilization_window=90 scale_up_cooldown=60` (pulled from control-plane).

sam: 90s window + 60s cooldown could definitely delay aggressive spin-up for short spikes. we'll propose reducing to 30/20 for bursty tenants.

olivia: logged a customer-facing note: proposing warm_pool_temp=2 + shorter stabilization for spikes. customer willing to test if it prevents errors.

maria: next steps — I will: 1) coordinate warm_pool bump with customer (in progress), 2) open infra ticket to look at registry pull backoffs (cc @infra), 3) adjust autoscaler config for controlled test and run ramp, 4) collect full attach/probe traces and share. tagging @jake @sam for followup. :thumbsup:

jake: thanks — if we can repro in-house with auth toggle + small warm pool we can iterate quickly. keep us posted.

sam: adding follow-up to eng-sre backlog to revisit default stabilization windows for Dedicated; file: DED-OPS-894.

maria: closing loop here when test done. assigning to support ticket #SUP-5421.

olivia: customer happy to co-test at 16:00 PT today. I'll coordinate. :spiral_calendar:
